title: The shop's own Net 10 term is due 10 days after the invoice date
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} holds the shop's own term {Term-A}, due 10 days after the invoice date.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-02 Customer and {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-02 Net 10.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is complete and ready to invoice (every part received, review done).
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-15440.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open {Work-order-1}'s Finance tab.
  2. Set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  3. Set Invoice Date to Oct 25, 2026.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice preview shows Invoice Date and Due date.
  • Step 2: the Due date reads Oct 15, 2026 (Oct 5 + 10 days).
  • Step 3: the Due date reads Nov 4, 2026 (Oct 25 + 10 days: 6 days to Oct 31, then 4).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R1: “A Net term (standard or the shop's own) is due that many days after the invoice date: an invoice dated Oct 5 on Net 30 is due Nov 4; on a shop's "Net 10" it is due Oct 15.”
  • Terminology: “The shop's own term → A term the shop created on the Credit Terms page, of one of two kinds: Due Net X days (due X days after the invoice date) or Due day of the following month (due on day X of the month after the invoice date).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
